method: Independent order_b incremental classification from the protocol and corpus only, with no supplied taxonomy or other-agent output. First infer and commit the Q09–Q16 tree in a visible reasoning checkpoint; freeze that snapshot. Then reconsider that existing tree with Q01–Q08, retaining all old questions, adding branches and moving Q15 to a new common parent. Each stage records a complete cumulative tree and assignments, while batch_ids records only the newly introduced batch. Labels describe requested operations/content, not a canonical subject hierarchy. Retained units reference exact source component IDs in declared order without paraphrasing payloads or generating answers. Validate both trees, cumulative coverage, unchanged first snapshot, null fields, and deterministic exact-source bundle assembly before exclusive output creation.

limitations: Original synthetic, pre-segmented sample of 16 questions only; not observed teacher demand, representative exams, or evidence of all-domain quality.

The corpus is one visible file, so later-batch content was accessible during reading; the first tree was explicitly reasoned and fixed before second-batch refinement, but this is not a blinded or mechanically gated exposure experiment.

The induced hierarchy is interpretive, not expert gold. Source interpretation and the algorithms/percentage parent are deliberate broad groupings; composite questions remain at parents rather than being forced into one leaf.
No comparison with another agent tree was performed; order sensitivity and final co-clustering comparison must be evaluated separately without treating labels as ground-truth accuracy.

Exact-ID resolution and deterministic source-bundle hash equality check reference completeness and assembly only, not AI extraction, source segmentation correctness, visual rendering, production storage, privacy, semantic correctness, or implementation readiness.
No source answers, rubrics or points were supplied; all remain null. No teacher taxonomy actions, paid calls, app API calls, or source edits were used.
No validation failures occurred in this run. Harness duration is not a production time/cost benchmark.
